name: Sequencing model — doc the priority/feature semantics + close the ordering gaps

current_round.prompt:
From: Buddy Williams <buddy.williams@insurity.com>
Subject: Sequencing model — doc the priority/feature semantics + close the ordering gaps

Body:
Team,

A user asked how to sequence work — "can feature 2 wait until feature 1 is
done, same for goals, and is it enforced across all nodes?" The pieces exist
but the intent docs don't state them plainly, and the implementation doesn't
yet fully deliver the intended priority-ordering guarantee. Two buckets.

--- Bucket 1: document what already works ---

1. Feature order is a HARD completion barrier for ordered goals within a
 feature: goal N+1 does not start until goal N reaches Review/Done/Cancelled;
 a failed ordered goal blocks the rest of the chain. State this explicitly in
 03-workflow and feature.md — today it only reads as "order matters when work
 has dependencies," which undersells it as a real gate.

2. Priority (low/medium/high) is meant to ENFORCE goal ordering, not just hint
 it. Document it as a hard selection gate: a lower-priority Todo is ineligible
 to start while a higher-priority Todo is eligible on the node. "Shape
 selection" in the overview undersells this — say "enforces start ordering."

--- Bucket 2: implementation gaps to close (behavior should match intent) ---

3. Priority ordering only gates status == Todo (priority_eligible, policy.rs).
 Once a high-priority goal leaves Todo (enters Plan/Implement) it drops out of
 highest_todo_rank, so a lower-priority Todo can start while the high-priority
 work is still in flight. If priority is meant to let users express "do A
 before B" without reaching for feature ordering, start-only gating isn't
 enough — the intended guarantee needs to hold across the goal's active
 lifecycle, not just at the Todo boundary. Treat this as the gap that makes
 feature-dependency feel like a workaround.

4. Ordering and priority are enforced per-node today (keyed on node_id in
 SchedulingEligibility). Not enforced across all nodes yet — intended to
 become global. Document current per-node scope AND the intended direction so
 users know to pin ordered work to one node in the meantime.

--- Design to state plainly (stop deferring it) ---

5. Dependencies are modeled AS the linear per-feature order, by design — "after
 X" and import depends_on intentionally compile down to that integer order;
 there is deliberately no separate DAG/blocked-by graph. The docs currently
 list "richer dependency reasoning" as Future Direction, which reads as
 unfinished work — replace that with a canonical statement that linear feature
 order (plus priority) IS the dependency model, so users stop hunting for a
 DAG feature that isn't coming.

Net user-facing answer these should make true and derivable:
- Goal ordering: priority enforces it (becoming global; per-node today).
- "A fully before B": feature order (completion barrier) today; priority
  should also express it once gap #3 is closed.
- Across all nodes: not yet — per-node today, global later.

Thanks,
Buddy

findings.description: P1 does not explicitly require documenting priority as a hard lifecycle gate: a lower-priority Todo is ineligible while higher-priority authored, Feature-eligible Todo or automated-active work exists on the same node, and becomes eligible only after that higher-priority work exits the active lifecycle.
findings.recommendation: Add the exact blocking and release rule to P1 alongside the current per-node and intended global scope.

findings.description: P1 names only the workflow and Feature pages, but docs/intent/02-model/02-models.md still advertises future dependency graphs, contradicting the requested canonical linear Feature order plus priority model with no separate DAG.
findings.recommendation: Include the affected model intent page and remove or clearly disambiguate its dependency-graph promise.

result.summary: The runtime plan is sound, but the documentation contract needs to state the exact priority gate and remove a conflicting DAG promise.

checklist.description: Revise the workflow overview, Feature surface intent, and model intent pages to define ordered Feature Goals as a hard barrier until the preceding Goal reaches Review, Done, or Cancelled, state that failure blocks later ordered Goals, specify that a lower-priority Todo is ineligible while higher-priority authored and Feature-eligible Todo or automated-active work exists on the same node and becomes eligible only after that work exits the active lifecycle, identify linear Feature order plus priority as the canonical dependency model with no separate DAG, and distinguish current per-node enforcement from intended global enforcement.

Move scheduling eligibility into a cohesive policy submodule and derive each node's blocking priority rank from every authored and Feature-eligible Todo or automated-active Goal, including runner-active Todo Goals, so already-active work continues while lower-priority Todo work remains unable to start until higher-priority work leaves the active lifecycle.

Add focused scheduling-policy coverage for every automated-active status, runner-active Todo work, release and terminal statuses, Feature-blocked higher-priority Goals, equal priorities, and distinct nodes to lock in the lifecycle barrier without implying cross-node enforcement.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: P1 now states the exact same-node hard gate, including which higher-priority Todo and automated-active work blocks a lower-priority Todo and that eligibility returns only after the blocking work exits the active lifecycle.

P1 now includes docs/intent/02-model/02-models.md and requires replacing its future dependency-graph promise with the canonical linear Feature order plus priority model and an explicit statement that no separate DAG exists.

result.summary: Document linear Feature order and priority as Refine's canonical hard sequencing model, then extend same-node priority enforcement across the active workflow lifecycle so lower-priority Todo work cannot start prematurely while the current per-node limitation remains explicit.

Moved SchedulingEligibility from policy/mod.rs into policy/scheduling_eligibility.rs. The per-node blocking_priority_rank now includes every authored, Feature-eligible Todo or automated-active Plan/Implement/Quality/Governance Goal. Removed runner-active exclusions while retaining the execution filter that lets active Goals continue.

Added seven focused scheduling-policy tests covering Plan, Implement, Quality, Governance, runner-active Todo semantics, Backlog/Review/Done/Failed/Cancelled release behavior, Feature-blocked high-priority work, equal priorities, distinct nodes, unauthored Todo work, and Feature release versus failed-chain blocking.
